title: Rebuilt my XAUUSD EA’s volume layer on GC futures. Looking for suggestions.
author: Solid-Promotion-7978
selftext:
Hi Experts,

I’ve been running an EA on XAUUSD M15 for a while. Recently I spent time on one weak spot: MT5’s XAUUSD volume is just the broker’s tick count, not real trades. So anything built on it (VWAP, volume profile, delta) is an approximation.

I moved that layer to CME gold futures (GC), where the volume is real. The EA reads the structure on GC (VWAP and bands, volume profile, IB, delta) and still trades on XAUUSD. The levels are converted with a futures-spot gap, measured as the median over the last 30 min. It skips a trade if the gap moved more than $1 in that window or if a contract roll happened in the last hour.

Testing: IS/OS over about 15 years, multiple regime checks, plus forward and live. The latest 5y 10m window (Jan 2021 – Oct 2026, every tick on real ticks) is in the screenshots:

It’s a backtest, so I know spread and slippage around the open are probably kinder here than live.

Where I’d like your input:

How do you handle the futures-spot gap? Is an empirical median fine, or is there a better fair-value or carry approach?  
How do you deal with contract rolls: skip a window or back-adjust?  
Is tick-level delta from GC good enough for a CFD, or is deeper order book data worth paying for?  
What haircut do you apply between tester and live fills on gold around the open?

Happy to share more on any part. Thanks for reading, and any criticism is welcome.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: on rolls I'd back-adjust for the levels and still skip the hour, because VWAP and the profile built across a roll mix two contracts' volume. the empirical median gap is fine as long as you check it doesn't drift with carry over a quarter.

comments.author: Goal_Pleasant
comments.body: Looks very good, in MT5 you can add spread or other changes to looks more real your backtest. Which strategy do you use to get a very good win rate in short trades with gold?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A Sharpe of 7.92 over about 10,000 trades with a 10 ms delay setting is the kind of result that depends heavily on fill assumptions, so my main suggestion is to re-run the same test with 200 to 500 ms delay and wider spreads and see where it breaks. For the gap, a rolling median is reasonable if you also log how it behaves around the open and scheduled releases (CPI, FOMC, NFP), when it widens most, so you can skip those windows or widen the check. For rolls, skipping a window is simpler than back-adjusting, since you only use the gap and not the old contract's price history. For the live haircut, measure your own live slippage by time of day and apply a multiple of it in the tester. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for tagging the news windows.
